sentences.text: The petitioners are the accused Nos. 1 to 4 in Crime No.212 of 2024 registered at the Venjaramoodu Police Station, for offences punishable under Sections 498A,323 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
The crime is registered on the complaint of the second respondent, who is none other than the wife of the first petitioner.
According to the defacto complainant, she was physically and mentally harassed by the petitioners after her marriage with the first petitioner on 15/01/2024.
The application for anticipatory bail filed by the petitioners before the Sessions Court was dismissed as per Annexure 5 order.
Hence, this bail application.

2. Learned Counsel for the petitioners contended that the allegations are patently false and the crime was got registered as a counter blast to the complaint filed by the first petitioner against the brother of the second respondent, as evidenced by Annexure 1.

On a specific query by the Court as to the observation in Annexure 5 order regarding a wound certificate produced from the side of the Sreeraj.S vs State Of Kerala on 6 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39847931/
2 defacto complainant to show that she was subjected to physical violence by the petitioner, learned Counsel submitted that no such incident, as alleged had happened and there is no such wound certificate also.

sentences.text: He further submitted that, as revealed from Annexure 3, it was the second respondent, who had slapped the first petitioner with her chappal, that too, while at the Police Station.
3. Learned Public Prosecutor submitted that, as per the statement of the second respondent, she was assaulted by the first petitioner and pursuant to her bleeding, was taken to a hospital.
In the body note prepared by the police at the hospital, contusion marks on her body were noted.
4. Going by the dates, events and also Annexure 3, I find prima facie merit in the contentions urged by the learned Counsel for the petitioners.
Pertinent to note that, despite service of notice and engaging a Counsel, neither the second respondent nor her Counsel has appeared before this Court.
Except the body note in which certain contusion marks are noted on the body of the second respondent, no wound certificate is made available.
In the above circumstances, custodial interrogation of the petitioners is not necessary.

Sd/-
